newsitem.title: UK: cricket-Astle over the moon about Notts contract.
newsitem.headline: cricket-Astle over the moon about Notts contract.

text.p: LONDON, June 3 - New Zealand cricket all-rounder Nathan Astle is not sure what skills his new club Nottinghamshire want him for, but he intends to make the most of his new three-month contract with the English county cricket side, NZPA reports.
Astle was signed by Notts today to fill their overseas player vacancy -- initially filled by Astle's New Zealand and Canterbury team-mate Chris Cairns, and then Pakistan fast bowler Mohammad Zahid.
Both players were released by the club because of injuries and international commitments, although Cairns will return next season.
Astle, 25, joined his new team-mates tonight and will make his English first-class debut tomorrow in a four-day match against Northamptonshire.
"I was over the moon," said Astle. "Everything's happened so quickly, I have no idea what I will be doing."
Astle said he was approached by Notts at the weekend after the club gained clearance from English cricketing authorities to opt out of the contract with Sahid, who had arrived with an injured back.
Zahid had replaced Cairns who had been signed by the club for two years but was released for 1997 because of an ankle injury and New Zealand team commitments.

Astle, who returned to England 10 days ago after playing for New Zealand in a one-day series in India, had been playing for Lancashire league club at Accrington but had always hoped to play county cricket one day.
He has not yet spoken with team management about his role with the club and does not know if he will be used primarily as a top-order batsmen or in a more all-round role.
Notts marketing manager Mark Arthur told NZPA that Astle fitted the club's requirements perfectly.
He said that when Cairns was released the club had wanted a fast bowler as a replacement but so far this season Notts had not scored enough runs.
He said Astle's batting ability, shown against England in New Zealand last summer, and his ability to score quickly in one-day games, had counted in his favour.
Astle scored a gritty century to deny England victory in the first test at Eden Park and more recently produced scores of 117, 92 and 9 in the Independence Cup one-day series in India.
Arthur said with two top-order batsmen already out of the side with broken bones in their hands, another run-maker was crucial and Notts had "no reservations" about Astle's abilities to do the job.
Astle will complete the season in England but will return to Canterbury before the New Zealand team tours Zimbabwe and Australia later this year.

Arthur said Cairn's contract for next year still stood, although it again carried a break clause that meant Notts could seek a replacement if the all-rounder was required for national duties for more than 28 days of the English season.
